text:
lee: Hey team, first week here. Trying to get kubectl working against the dev cluster. `kubectl get ns` -> You must be logged in to the server (Unauthorized). KUBECONFIG is ~/.kube/config. Who should I ping for the typical onboarding flow?

infra-bot: Welcome! :wave: Standard flow: 1) redwood-cli auth sso --provider okta 2) redwood-cli kubeconfig fetch --env dev 3) kubectl config use-context redwood-dev. See https://redwood.internal/onboarding/kubernetes

toni: hey lee, welcome. If your browser is locked down use `redwood-cli auth sso --device-code` then `redwood-cli kubeconfig fetch`. After fetch run `kubectl config get-contexts` and `kubectl config current-context`.

lee: thanks toni. I ran the device flow and see `redwood-dev` in contexts but when I do `kubectl get pods -n data-platform` I get `forbidden: User "github|lee" cannot list resource "pods" in namespace "data-platform"`. What namespace access do new hires get by default?

sylvia: welcome! By default you get view on `default` and `platform-dev`. For anything else file a request in #help or ping eng-infra. If it's for onboarding we usually grant a short-lived view role (6-24h). Include your GitHub username and namespaces.

lee: pinging here: GH handle `leeh` and need view for `data-platform` to follow the runbook.

toni: I'll add you to the `k8s-dev-readers` group and grant view on `data-platform` for 12h. One thing to check: if you have other kubeconfigs (minikube, cloud CLIs) they may override. Use `kubectl config view --minify` to see the user/cert used for the current context.

lee: that fixed it, can list pods now. Quick follow-up: any recommended local shortcuts for switching contexts?

sylvia: I use aliases: `kc() { kubectl --context=$1 "$@"; }` then `kc redwood-dev get pods -n data-platform`. Also `kubens` helps for switching namespaces.

lee: great tips, thanks all! One last ask: where's the policy for requesting elevated access for debugging?

infra-bot: Link: https://redwood.internal/policies/k8s-elevation. Temporary elevation requires a reason, ticket ID, and approver. Approved durations are logged.

lee: perfect, appreciate the help :smile:
